subject: Availability floor & credit escrow mechanics — proposed amendment
messages:
From: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@equusplatform.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed SLA amendment for migration window

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we line up the Equus migration (target cutover Oct 1), our legal and ops teams want a short-term tweak to the standard SLA to mitigate risk during the ramp. Two asks: 

1) Availability floor: for the first 60 days post-cutover, allow a lowered availability floor of 99.9% (instead of 99.95%). This is just for the initial warm-up where we expect traffic spikes and cache miss patterns.

2) Monthly credit escrow: instead of immediate payout for any remedy, propose an escrow approach where up to 20% of the monthly invoice can be held as potential credits and reconciled within 30 days. That helps us budget and keeps the commercial invoice predictable.

Attached is our proposed redline showing the exact wording and a short spreadsheet with example calculations. Can Redwood provide a counter? We can be flexible on precise % caps but would like clarity on measurement (UTC day boundaries) and carveouts for scheduled maintenance.

Would appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement is on a tight timeline.

Thanks,
Alex Ruiz
Head of Platform Operations
Equus Platform

[Attachment: Equus_SLA_Redwood_Amendments.pdf (pdf)]

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@equusplatform.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed SLA amendment for migration window

Alex —

Appreciate the clear ask and the redline. We want Equus to have a smooth cutover; below are Redwood's suggested changes so we can move quickly without opening risk across our book of business: 

- Availability floor: we can agree to a temporary 60-day graceband that uses a 99.90% availability threshold for credit calculation only. Important: the baseline availability in contract remains 99.95% (so our long-term commercial baseline is unchanged). The temporary floor triggers a different credit multiplier (see below).

- Monthly credit escrow: we are open to an escrow-style reconciliation, but propose capping escrow at 15% of the month invoice rather than 20% to align with our risk profile. Escrowed amounts will be held for up to 30 days pending final measurement and then applied or released.

- Carveouts & measurement: Redwood will exclude scheduled maintenance windows >1 hour if notified 72 hours in advance and any agreed force majeure. Measurement window will use UTC day boundaries, per your note.

- Credit mechanics (proposal): for the temporary 60-day period only, monthly remedy = min(invoice_month_total * 0.15, downtime_hours * hourly_rate_equivalent * 10). After the 60-day period, standard remedy table (as in our template) applies.

If that looks reasonable, we can present the wording to Legal and produce a redline. Marissa/Karthik — tagging you for any technical or commercial concerns.

Cheers,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

[Attachment: none]

From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@equusplatform.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@equusplatform.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 10:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed SLA amendment for migration window

Mateo / Marissa,

Thanks for the quick reply. A couple of clarifications from Legal / Procurement so we can sign-off internally: 

- Cap: 15% cap is closer to acceptable, but our CFO will push back unless we see example math showing worst-case exposure. Can Redwood provide a 3-line example using a $120k monthly invoice showing (a) no downtime, (b) 0.05% below baseline, (c) full 99.5% hit to show the payout in dollars? That will help our treasury team.

- Measurement: UTC boundaries are fine. Please explicitly confirm that transient errors (5xx spikes under 1 minute) will be aggregated into the hourly buckets before crediting (we don’t want noise to create immediate payouts).

- DocuSign / timing: procurement needs the final doc by next Wed (2026-09-15) to keep our migration schedule. If Redwood requires leadership sign-off for the 15% escrow cap, please escalate; otherwise propose the redline and we’ll get our counsel to review.

Attached a quick spreadsheet with sample calculations and a suggested revision to the escrow clause (Equus_Credit_Sample.xlsx).

Best,
Sara Kim
Senior Counsel — Equus Platform

[Attachment: Equus_Credit_Sample.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@equusplatform.com>, Sara Kim <sara.kim@equusplatform.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed SLA amendment for migration window

Marissa / Karthik —

Quick summary and ask: Equus is willing to accept a 15% escrow cap but wants concrete example math and confirmation on transient aggregation. They also need the final contract back by 2026-09-15. My recommended path to close: 

1) Provide the 3-line example Sara requested (I can draft numbers today).
2) Approve a 60-day temporary graceband at 99.90% for credit calculation only, with the 15% escrow cap and a simple hourly-aggregation rule for transient spikes (aggregate 5xxs into 15-minute buckets; buckets under 1 minute ignored).

Commercial concession I recommend we accept if Leadership signs off: allow the temporary floor for 60 days (not 90), escrow cap 15%, explicit maintenance carveouts, and a one-time implementation credit equal to 10% off the first invoice if Equus commits to a 12-month term. That implementation credit is bounded to reduce churn risk and helps them buy down migration costs.

Karthik — can you confirm there are no infra/ops reasons we shouldn’t accept the 60-day temporary floor? Marissa — can you and your team produce the example calculations and the redline wording by EOD Monday so we can route to Legal? If leadership approval is needed I’ll escalate this morning.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
